detail:
Sources describe compression garments as a way to counteract blood pooling in the lower body. Mayo Clinic recommends garments that "mildly compress the thighs and abdomen" as a way to encourage proper blood flow and reduce symptoms. Harvard Health's review cites a study showing that an abdominal binder combined with knee-high socks provides the best results. American Nurse Today adds that garments should ideally compress the calf, thigh, and lower abdomen, and notes that "leg compression alone tends to be less effective."

Compression is presented as a supportive, non-pharmacologic measure alongside other management steps. Talk to your doctor about whether compression garments are appropriate for you and which type to use.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material.
